method: Each section read in full by a machine-assisted reviewer against the packs and the ground catalogue as of this date; not a legal review.

sections.bearsOn: Defines Crown land, disposition, reserved land, natural boundary and right of way; the On this ground screens rely on "disposition" and "right of way" to say what a Land Act tenure is.
Excludes Public Agency Accommodation Act land from "Crown land".
Cabinet constitutes land districts.
Cabinet constitutes land recording districts.
The minister administers Crown land not under another ministry.
Minister responsible for geographical names.
Minister responsible for base mapping and land information systems.
The Crown land registry (Tantalis) records Crown land dispositions but not forest service roads, timber harvesting agreements or range tenures, so a Tantalis read under a block will not show those.
Defines tenure and tenure authority for the Integrated Land and Resource Registry.
Minister maintains the Integrated Land and Resource Registry; tenure authorities submit tenure information to it.
Information in the integrated registry is not notice to anyone.
Public electronic access to the integrated registry, with restrictions.
No liability for reliance on the integrated registry.
Repealed; no operative text.
Offence Act s. 5 does not apply to Part 1.1.
Regulations prescribing tenures and information for the integrated registry.
An application gives no right or priority to Crown land, and a disposition binds the government only once executed; a Land Act application under a block is not yet a tenure.
Citizenship requirement for a Crown grant.
Who may apply for Crown land; the minister may refuse an application over land reserved under s. 15 or withdrawn under s. 16.
Minister may order that no Land Act application be made for an area, activity, use, period or class of applicant.

The minister may sell or lease Crown land, grant rights of way and easements and licences to occupy, on terms the minister sets; the terms of such a tenure over a block govern what the holder may do there.
Crown grant of cancelled dedicated land to a petitioner.
A road designated in a Land Act disposition is deemed 20 m wide (10 m each side of centreline) and stays Crown land.
Repealed; no operative text.

Cabinet may reserve Crown land from disposition for a public purpose, on terms, but a licence of occupation for a road may still be issued over it; the reserve does not itself regulate forest practices, but its terms may restrict use of the land under a block.
sections.gapNote: The pack asks whether a reserve exists but tests only §17 designation terms for restrictions; terms attached to a §15 order in council are not asked about.
proposedFacts: Do the terms of the Land Act §15 order reserving this land restrict harvesting, road construction or reforestation on the block?

sections.bearsOn: The minister may temporarily withdraw Crown land from disposition and impose terms on its use; the terms, not the withdrawal itself, may bear on activity under a block.
sections.gapNote: The pack records a withdrawal but does not ask whether terms imposed under §16(3) restrict the proposed harvest, roads or planting.
proposedFacts: Do terms imposed on the Land Act §16 withdrawal restrict harvesting, road construction or reforestation on the block?

sections.bearsOn: The minister may designate Crown land for a use or for conservation, impose terms on its use, and withdraw it from incompatible dispositions; designation terms may restrict forest work on a block.
Land below the natural boundary of water is not Crown granted except by order.
Land suited to quarrying or gravel is not Crown granted except by order.
520 ha limit on a Crown grant.
520 ha limit on a lease, except grazing and other listed purposes.
60 year limit on a lease term.
Crown land suitable for timber production is not Crown granted unless the minister finds it needed for agricultural settlement or a higher economic use.
A Land Act disposition may require payment for the timber on the land.
Crown grant may issue before full payment if secured.
Interest on deferred payments.
Reservations to which a certificate of purchase is subject, including existing roads and trails.
Royalty on gravel, rock and other construction materials removed under a disposition.
Survey fees.
Minister may vary the area under application.
Transfer of Crown land administration to Canada.
Applications for purchase, lease, licence, easement or right of way are made to the minister and published online once accepted.
Minister may require public notice of an application.
Public comments on an application before a disposition.
A minor may hold a disposition.
Applicant may be required to file studies, timber cruises and pay assessment costs.
Security may be required of an applicant.
Applicant must supply information; false statements are an offence.
The minister may issue a lease on terms, including an option to purchase; a grazing lease's terms decide what forest work it allows on the leased ground.
The minister may issue a licence of occupation on terms.
The minister may grant rights of way and easements over Crown land on terms; a right of way crossing a block may limit clearing or roads within it.
Application may be disallowed if the survey is not completed.
Date of a disposition is the date it is executed.
Cancellation of a disposition for default.
Amendment or cancellation of an improper approval or grant.
Abandonment of a disposition.
Debts survive cancellation.
Land in a cancelled disposition may be withheld for up to a year.
Issue of a Crown grant on payment.
Where a Crown grant reserved the timber to the government and no one holds it, the minister may grant the timber to the owner once its stumpage value is paid.
Statutory exceptions and reservations in every disposition (resumption for public works, minerals, water, and road materials including timber).
Crown grants to government bodies.
Deleting terms from Crown grants.
Cancelling and correcting defective grants.
Delivery and registration of Crown grants.
Beds of water bodies do not pass with a Crown grant.
Application of s. 55.
Roads shown on a Crown grant plan stay Crown land, deemed 20 m wide.
Declaration including a water body or road in a subdivision.
Minister's remedies for trespass on Crown land.
Offences: occupying or using Crown land, or building or excavating on it, without lawful authority.
Enforcement of trespass payments.
Liability for s. 60 contraventions.
Repealed; the range of sections holds no text in force.
Holder of a disposition may sue for trespass.
Cabinet may prohibit a use of Crown land in a designated area by regulation; contravention is an offence.
Dumping garbage or other substances on Crown land prohibited.
General penalty.
Survey of district lots.
Repealed; the range of sections holds no text in force.
Surveys must be confirmed by the Surveyor General.
Survey rules.
Only BC land surveyors carry out surveys.
Cancelling a survey and ordering a resurvey.
Minister may order a survey.
Surveyor General's survey instructions.
Survey instructions for treaty lands.
Survey may be rejected.
Road and walkway allowances.
Road allowance to private land being subdivided.
Agreed boundary replacing a natural boundary.
Reposting surveys.
Resurvey to replace a boundary.
Resurvey for lost posts.
Limits on resurvey powers.
Notice and hearing for resurvey.
Hearing of protest.
Confirmation of resurvey plan.
Deposit of resurvey plan.
Resurvey binding.
Compensation for land gained or lost on resurvey.
Cost of resurvey.
Recovery of resurvey costs.
Defines "official" for Part 7.1.
Part 7.1 and orders under it bind the government, so objectives bind BC Timber Sales as well.
Sections 93.4 and 93.7 do not apply in the Haida Gwaii management area.
Not in force: the sections are enacted but have not been brought into force, so they bind nothing.

The minister may by order establish objectives for Crown resources and Crown land (and TFL, woodlot and community forest private land) for the purposes of FRPA; this is how Omineca land use orders such as the 2006 ADA/SRA orders and the Mackenzie LRMP objectives bind blocks through forest stewardship plans.
sections.gapNote: The Omineca orders are now rules in their own packs (the 2006 ADA/SRA order, the old growth orders, the Mackenzie biodiversity order and the visual quality orders), which cite the orders themselves; the ground screens cite s. 93.4. A legal OGMA under an order not transcribed (the Robson Valley orders, among others) raises old growth 1.2.0's ogma-other-order on s. 93.4 and leaves the order's objectives to the reviewer.

sections.bearsOn: A minister's §93.4 objective must be consistent with Cabinet designations and objectives under ss. 93.1 and 93.3, which prevail in a conflict.
sections.gapNote: Where a Cabinet designation or objective and a minister's order overlap a block, the pack does not say which prevails; rare in the Omineca.
proposedFacts: Does a Cabinet designation or objective under Land Act §93.1 or §93.3 apply to the block alongside a minister's order, and do they conflict?

sections.bearsOn: Proposed §93.4 objectives must be made public for review and comment unless urgent.
Delegation of the minister's §§93.4 to 93.6 powers; continues Forest Practices Code delegations.

Objectives set under Forest Practices Code Act ss. 3 to 5 for resource management zones, landscape units or sensitive areas continue as §93.4 objectives; the 2004 Prince George TSA biodiversity order and the 2001 to 2003 OGMA orders bind through this section.
sections.gapNote: The OGMA screen now cites s. 93.8, and the Omineca old growth pack holds the rules of the Dome/Slim, Humbug and Obo/Fox orders it continues.
proposedFacts: Does the block or its road overlap an old growth management area or other objective established under the Forest Practices Code and continued under Land Act §93.8?
If a road must cross a legal OGMA, has it been shown that there is no other practicable option and how will the road be deactivated and the area replaced?
